d: The healer who could not bear the burn. A student of the protocol who refused Stage 4 and built a civilisation on the promise that nothing will ever be destroyed, changed, or felt again. She calls it mercy.
kit: STHITI BANDHAN · TRIKAALVALEX · THE NISHCHAL ORDER

powers.lore: She was a healer first. That is the part Sthavantum never puts on a wall. She reached Stage 4, felt what the burn asks of you, and refused it — then built an entire civilisation so that no one would ever have to be asked again. Sthiti Bandhan holds a person exactly where they are. Nothing destroyed, nothing changed, nothing felt. She calls it mercy, and she has never once said the other word for it.

ordinaryLife.lore: This track has not been filmed yet.

d: The true believer. Where Tamasa built the empire from a personal flinch, Meralaine believes in stillness as a philosophy — that feeling is a wound and the kind thing is to end it. More dangerous than Tamasa because he has no guilt: he runs the clinics that turn citizens into stilled ones, and he sleeps perfectly.
style: Flawless indigo corporate tailoring, frost-blue subdermal interface lines, a voice engineered to lower the heart-rate of anyone who hears it. Beautiful the way a sealed room is beautiful.
kit: Master of the Sthiti Bandhan binding-code; a vocal synthesiser calibrated to induce compliance; command of the stilling clinics. He does not fight — he settles.
root: The preserving function (Sthiti) as seduction; the cold mirror of Uma’s bliss.

powers.lore: Tamasa built the empire from a flinch. Meralaine built his from conviction, which is worse. He runs the stilling clinics and believes every hour of it: that feeling is a wound, that ending it is kindness, that the settled face on the table is a person rescued. His voice is calibrated to be agreed with. He does not fight anyone. He settles them, goes home, and sleeps perfectly.

d: "The hall of the god." Devashaley genuinely believes suppression is holy — that to still a soul is to protect it from the violence of change. The Order is his cathedral and the stilled ones are his congregation; he is the theological engine that lets ordinary people participate in cruelty and call it faith.
style: Austere ceremonial obsidian; a still, hall-like presence. Where Meralaine is corporate, Devashaley is clerical — the priest of the frozen god.
kit: Doctrinal authority; command of the Order’s enforcement rites; the Bhairava invocation as an instrument of "mercy." Controls who gets stilled and who gets erased.
root: Deva (god) + shala (hall) — the house of a god who has stopped moving.

powers.lore: The hall of the god. Devashaley gives cruelty its liturgy — the rites, the invocation, the language that lets an ordinary person hold someone down and call it faith. The Order is his cathedral and the stilled ones are his congregation. He decides who is merely stilled and who is erased, and he has never experienced that decision as anything but holy.

ordinaryLife.lore: This track has not been filmed yet.

d: A poet before the Order took him. Kavijyana knows the Raktabija Protocol proves the whole system is a lie, because he is the one who keeps deleting the proof. The cold world’s most likely defector and its most valuable one — he carries the numbers that could bring Sthavantum down.
style: Understated frost-blue; ink-stained interface gloves; the tired eyes of someone who writes lies for a living and remembers when he wrote truth.
kit: Total access to Sahasragard’s vaults; narrative-control tooling; the ability to make a relapse-cascade disappear from every record in an afternoon.
root: Kavi (seer-poet) + jnana (knowledge) — knowledge forced to serve its own suppression.

powers.lore: He was a poet before the Order found a better use for him. Now he has the vaults of Sahasragard and the tooling to make a relapse-cascade vanish from every record before evening. Which means Kavijyana knows, more precisely than anyone alive, that the Raktabija Protocol proves the whole system is a lie — because he is the one who keeps deleting the proof. He still has the numbers. He has not decided what he is.

d: "Without refuge." Anisraya was made the way Virabhadra was made — spun from a single act of severed grief, given a body and a purpose and no home to return to. Deployed against the warm world’s field-guardians. The cruellest question the story asks: can something manufactured from another’s wound be healed, or only released?
style: Grey-on-obsidian combat frame; no ornament, no expression, exposed enforcement-cybernetics. Moves without the small hesitations that mark a person who has a self to protect.
kit: Severance-grade combat cyberware; a strike-fist that installs the Sthiti Bandhan on contact, caging a target mid-motion; total obedience to Bhairacrux command.
root: An-ashraya (without refuge) + Virabhadra, the wrath-born from Shiva’s severed lock.

powers.lore: Without refuge. Made the way Virabhadra was made — spun out of one act of severed grief, handed a body, a purpose, and nowhere to return to. The severance-grade cyberware is only the delivery system; the strike-fist installs Sthiti Bandhan on contact and cages a field-guardian mid-motion. She obeys Bhairacrux completely. The question the story will not let go of: can a thing manufactured from someone else's wound be healed, or only released?

d: A walking Raktabija Protocol — a stilled one who relapsed, spawned, and slipped the net, then turned around and started selling the very sedative that broke him. He hates the Order and depends on it: the clearest street-level evidence that Tamasa’s system manufactures its own black market.
style: Low-sector frost-blue grime; a kiosk-runner’s hunch; interface-scars from too many cheap stilling-sessions.
kit: A supply line of black-market Vasvishantum; contacts in Nishchalwick Kiosk; the survival-cunning of someone the system used up and spat out.
root: The relapse-duplicate that escaped; the -wick vendor-suffix of the cold streets.

powers.lore: A walking Raktabija Protocol. Stilled, relapsed, spawned, slipped the net — and then turned around and started moving the same sedative that broke him. He hates the Order with his whole chest and cannot eat without it. Black-market Vasvishantum, contacts down at Nishchalwick Kiosk, and the specific cunning of someone the system used up and spat out. Tamasa's civilisation manufactures its own black market. Mehlowick is the receipt.

d: "Trishna" — thirst. What the system produces when it stills a person incompletely and then offers the sedative as the only relief: an operative whose loyalty is chemical. Tamasa’s failure wearing a uniform. If the warm world could complete her interrupted heal, they would turn the Order’s own craving-engine against it.
style: Elegant decay: expensive cold-world dress worn thin, frost-blue interface flickering with withdrawal. The face of someone always mid-reach for the next stilling.
kit: Deniable wetwork; an intimate knowledge of the clinics from the inside; a dependency the Order exploits as leverage — she works to be stilled again.
root: Trishna (craving) — the thirst the cold world manufactures and feeds.

powers.lore: Trishna. Thirst. This is what the system produces when it stills a person halfway and then offers the sedative as the only way down: an operative whose loyalty is chemical. She knows the clinics from the inside, does the work the Order cannot be seen doing, and takes her payment in being stilled again. She is Tamasa's failure wearing a uniform — and if the warm world ever completed her interrupted heal, the Order's craving-engine would turn on it.

d: Low-level market informant; sells small-time intel, always on the clock.
kit: A market stall’s worth of small-time intel, metered and always on the clock; kiosk contacts across the low sectors.

d: Fragment-keeper trading partial files and severed case-records; the memory-broker.
kit: Partial files and severed case-records; can reassemble a fragment the Order meant to lose.

d: Hardened fixer at the border edge — unbending, unafraid, unbought.
kit: Border-edge contacts on both sides of the seam, and a standing reputation for staying unbought.
